prompt:
Feature: add centiliter to the seeded ingredient units.

Centiliters (cl, a hundredth of a liter, ten milliliters) are common in European recipes, but the English (en-US) unit seed data has no centiliter. A unit called "cl" is therefore not recognised as a standard unit and gets no standardized amount, so it cannot be converted the way milliliters and liters can.

Expected:
- The en-US unit seed data gets a centiliter entry, keyed "centiliter", with the name "centiliter", the plural name "centiliters", the abbreviation "cl" and an empty description, like its neighbours. Seeding units for en-US then also creates "centiliter".
- When a unit is created without a standard set by the user, the unit repository standardizes it from its name, plural name, abbreviation or plural abbreviation (case-insensitive), as today, by setting standard_unit (a StandardizedUnitType) and standard_quantity. Centiliter joins that table: a unit created with the name "cl" (SaveIngredientUnit(name="cl")) comes back standardized, so that converting it to the other volume units works. The other standard units keep their values.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests/repository_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
title: feat: add centiliter to seeded ingredient units (#8766)
